column1: # T-GATES-047 timing-bound test list: every #[test] function whose verdict the scan ties to the real clock. Three shapes:

# (1) its own body waits (sleep, sleep_ms, recv_timeout, wait_timeout, wait_timeout_ms, wait_timeout_while, park_timeout, park_timeout_ms: stable std; WaitForSingleObject(Ex), WaitForMultipleObjects(Ex), MsgWaitForMultipleObjects(Ex), SignalObjectAndWait, SleepEx, Sleep, WaitNamedPipeW, GetQueuedCompletionStatus(Ex), GetOverlappedResultEx, WinHttpSetTimeouts, WaitForInputIdle, WaitForDebugEvent(Ex), SleepConditionVariableSRW/CS, WaitOnAddress, CoWaitForMultipleHandles, WSAPoll, WSAWaitForMultipleEvents: Win32; CFRunLoopRunInMode, CFRunLoop::run_in_mode: macOS; set_read_timeout, set_write_timeout, connect_timeout: std sockets; each by its called name, whatever its bound; libc::poll, ppoll, select, pselect, kevent, epoll_wait, nanosleep, usleep, pthread_cond_timedwait, sem_timedwait, clock_nanosleep, sigtimedwait and WinSock::select: by the call of their path, plan row 163) or measures (elapsed);
# (2) its own body does clock arithmetic between two different Instant::now()/SystemTime::now() readings (T-TIMING-BOUND-STRAYS);

# (3) it reaches, through resolved call-graph edges, a test-only helper of its target that waits or measures as (1) or (2) say, at any depth (T-TIMING-BOUND-STRAYS: a kept measurement; widened by T-TIMING-GUARD-FOLLOWS-WAITING-HELPERS: any wait, a stall timer, a zero bound) - except through a door, a helper that is itself a row: the walk stops there, and the tests that reach it are not rows through it.
# bt-source's timing test holds the tree to this list both ways; scripts/ci/check-timing-bound.ps1 lets whole
# rows only disappear against the merge base, except for the rows a new widening line admits by count. A real-time window in
# product code is not seen by the scan: a product function's own Instant::now()/SystemTime::now()/elapsed() deadline or bound,
# its own std wait (recv_timeout, wait_timeout*, park_timeout*) on a Duration read from no clock, its own kernel wait (WaitFor*,
# MsgWaitFor*, WaitNamedPipeW, GetQueuedCompletionStatus, a socket's or WinHTTP's timeout, libc::poll) on a constant, handed or
# clock-derived bound, or a Duration a test hands to a product wait. The walk ends at the first product function, and that a test reaches a product clock decides nothing about
# whether another thread acts inside its window. Plan row 125 swept bt-app and bt-platform by hand on 2026-10-31 at 9ac40b223,
# plan row 153 swept the std waits on 2026-11-01 at 417b32f65, and plan row 163 swept bt-platform's kernel waits on 2026-11-02
# at f641b0064 (their `# noted` lines below); review owns any window added since. A `# noted` line records such a clock found and closed by review: it moves no row.
# widened 2026-10-24 by T-TIMING-BOUND-STRAYS (+20 rows): clock arithmetic in a test's own body, a budget measured in a test-only helper
